body:
WHAT
Scripts get two helpers. `pipeline(items, ...stages)` runs each item through all stages on its own, so item 3 can be in stage 2 while item 1 is still in stage 1 — there is no waiting point between stages. `parallel([thunks])` runs all thunks and waits for every one before returning. In both, a stage or thunk that throws produces `null` for that slot instead of failing the whole run.

WHY
One slow item must never hold up the rest, and one failing subagent must not throw away every other result.

WHERE
engine/core/src/scheduling/workflow.ts — the `pipeline` and `parallel` hooks defined inside `WorkflowRunner.run()` (per-item `for (const stage of stageFns)` with try/catch → null; `Promise.all` over thunks with try/catch → null); they are passed to the script via `new AsyncFunction('agent','parallel','pipeline','phase','log','args','budget', body)`.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. pipeline([a,b], stage1, stage2) where stage1 for `a` is slow: record the order of stage entries and assert stage2 for `b` starts before stage1 for `a` finishes (no barrier).
2. parallel([slowThunk, fastThunk]) resolves only after both settle, and the result array preserves thunk order regardless of finish order.
3. pipeline where stage2 throws for item 1 only returns [null, result2] and the run result is ok:true.
4. parallel where one thunk rejects returns null in that position and the other values intact; the run result is ok:true.
5. pipeline(nonArray) and parallel(nonArray) throw with the 'expects an array' message, which surfaces as {ok:false, error} for the run.
